fhb-low-deposit.html: In Sep 2026, 50.3% of First Home Buyer mortgages approved across New Zealand (55.6% by dollar value, or $850m) had under a 20% deposit (+4.2 pts YoY).
fhb-low-deposit.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C31, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Percentages & averages derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only.

fhb-share.html: First Home Buyers accounted for 20.3% of all new NZ mortgage lending in Sep 2026 (2,667 home loans approved, average loan $574k; +1.1 pts YoY).
fhb-share.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C31, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Percentages & averages derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only.

investors.html: Property investors accounted for 17.7% of new NZ mortgage lending in Sep 2026 ($1.33B; -3.5 pts YoY), compared with 20.3% for First Home Buyers.
investors.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C31, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Percentages & averages derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only.

refinance.html: Moving banks is a regular part of the New Zealand mortgage market rather than a rare step—in September 2026 alone, 2,772 borrowers switched mortgage providers, moving $1.73B in loans (23.0% of all new lending, at an average loan size of $624k).
refinance.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C33, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only, not personalised financial advice.

top-ups.html: Many Kiwi homeowners tap into existing equity for renovations or upgrades rather than moving house—in September 2026, 9,639 borrowers topped up an existing mortgage, making up 46.4% of all mortgage approvals by count (average top-up: $100k).
top-ups.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C33, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only, not personalised financial advice.

settled-rates.html: Advertised bank rates only tell half the story—across all new fixed mortgages actually settled in September 2026, New Zealand borrowers locked in a weighted-average rate of 4.82% for one year and 5.09% for two years.
settled-rates.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table B30, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Historical market statistics for general information only.

rent-yield-pulse.html: Private weekly rents across New Zealand have been relatively steady over the past year—the national median sat at $595/wk in August 2026 (up 0.8% on a year earlier), with regional medians at $650/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $550/wk in Canterbury.
rent-yield-pulse.source_html: Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data), licensed under CC BY 3.0 NZ. Derived by HLF. Historical market statistics only.

rental-bonds-supply.html: Thousands of New Zealand households sign new leases every month—Tenancy Services logged 13,062 newly lodged private rental bonds in August 2026, across a nationwide pool of 522,942 active private tenancies.
rental-bonds-supply.source_html: Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data), licensed under CC BY 3.0 NZ. Derived by HLF. Historical market statistics only.

student-loan-servicing.html: Student debt is a familiar line item on home loan applications—across Inland Revenue's June 2026 figures, the median NZ student loan balance sat at $18,301 (up 4.5% on a year earlier), where compulsory PAYE deductions factor into how banks test monthly servicing.
student-loan-servicing.source_html: Source: Inland Revenue — Student Loan Statistics (Jun 2026), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Servicing context by HLF for general information only.

kiwisaver-first-home.html: For many buyers, KiwiSaver does much of the heavy lifting toward a first deposit—in September 2026, 4,250 members withdrew a combined $195.7m to put toward a first home, or roughly $46k per withdrawing member.
kiwisaver-first-home.source_html: Source: Inland Revenue — KiwiSaver Withdrawal Statistics, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Derived by HLF for general information only.

kiwisaver-switches.html: Reviewing and changing KiwiSaver providers happens more regularly than many members realise—over the year to June 2026, 198,897 New Zealanders moved their balance to a new scheme, averaging 16,575 switches every month.
kiwisaver-switches.source_html: Source: Inland Revenue — KiwiSaver Scheme Transfer Statistics (CC BY 4.0). Monthly average derived by HLF. General information only, not personalised KiwiSaver advice.

new-builds-annual.html: New-build supply across New Zealand has been gathering pace, with 41,091 new homes consented in the year to September 2026 (up 18.0% on the previous year, including 3,570 dwellings consented in September 2026).
new-builds-annual.source_html: Source: Stats NZ — Building Consents Issued (September 2026), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Multi-unit share derived by HLF. Historical market statistics only.

townhouse-share.html: Townhouses and multi-unit developments now make up more than half of new residential consents—accounting for 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570 homes) consented in September 2026, including 1,305 townhouses, flats, and units.
townhouse-share.source_html: Source: Stats NZ — Building Consents Issued (September 2026), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Multi-unit share derived by HLF. Historical market statistics only.

build-cost-inflation.html: Residential build-cost inflation has settled into single digits compared with the post-pandemic construction surge—Stats NZ recorded a +3.2% annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home in the September 2026 quarter, alongside 3.7% overall CPI inflation.
build-cost-inflation.source_html: Source: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (September 2026 quarter), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Historical market statistics only.
